---
title: "Getting started"
---

This chapter takes you from nothing to a published page: install the tool, set up
a kernel for code, write your first document, and put it online.

## Install

qmd-fast builds from source with a Rust toolchain. From the repo:

```sh
cargo build --release
```

The binary is `target/release/qmd-fast`. The repo also ships a `~/.local/bin/qmd-fast`
launcher that rebuilds the release binary whenever the tool's sources change and
then runs it, so once it's on your `PATH` you can just say `qmd-fast preview …`
from any directory. Every command below works either way — substitute
`cargo run -p qmd-fast-server --` for `qmd-fast` if you prefer not to install the
launcher.

## Set up a kernel (for code execution)

Prose, math, diagrams, and Observable cells need no setup. To *execute*
`{python}` / `{r}` cells you point the server at a Jupyter kernel. A one-time
Python setup:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install ipykernel numpy matplotlib   # + whatever your cells import
export QMD_FAST_PYTHON="$(pwd)/.venv/bin/python"
```

For R cells, install `IRkernel` and set `QMD_FAST_R`. Without a kernel, cells
render as highlighted source and the preview shows a quiet "kernel unavailable"
note instead of failing — so you can always start writing and add a kernel later.

## Your first document

Create `hello.qmd`:

````markdown
---
title: "Hello, qmd-fast"
toc: true
---

# Introduction

A paragraph with **markdown**, inline math $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$, and a diagram:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  write --> preview --> publish
```

# Compute

```{python}
import numpy as np
np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=5).round(2)
```
````

Preview it live:

```sh
qmd-fast preview hello.qmd
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4321`. Edit the file and watch only the changed block
update in place. Double-click any block to jump to its source line in your
editor.

## Build for publishing

When you're happy, `build` produces output (executing code cells against the
kernel, so the HTML carries the computed figures):

```sh
qmd-fast build hello.qmd                 # -> hello.html (one self-contained file)
qmd-fast build hello.qmd --out dist      # -> dist/index.html + copied local assets
```

Point `build`/`preview` at a **directory** instead and you get a whole
multi-page site or book (see [Slides, books & sites](formats.qmd)):

```sh
qmd-fast build blog/                     # -> blog/_site/   (one .html per page)
qmd-fast build docs/                     # -> docs/_book/   (a book, if _quarto.yml says so)
```

## Publish it

The build output is **plain static HTML + assets** with no server runtime, so it
deploys anywhere that serves files.

- **GitHub Pages.** Build into `docs/` (or push `_site/`) on your default branch
  and enable Pages, or use an action that runs `qmd-fast build` and uploads the
  output directory as the Pages artifact.
- **Netlify / Vercel / Cloudflare Pages.** Set the build command to
  `cargo run -p qmd-fast-server -- build <dir>` and the publish directory to the
  emitted `_site/` / `_book/`.
- **Any static host / `rsync`.** Copy the output folder as-is. The `--out <dir>`
  form and the site/book builds copy referenced local assets next to the HTML, so
  the folder is self-contained.

### Deploy with GitHub Actions

A copy-paste workflow that builds on every push and publishes to GitHub Pages.
Enable **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions** once, then drop this in
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:

```yaml
name: Deploy
on:
  push: { branches: [main] }
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write
concurrency: { group: pages, cancel-in-progress: true }

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Install qmd-fast
        # point at wherever qmd-fast lives; add --tag vX.Y for reproducible builds
        run: cargo install --git https://github.com/you/qmd-fast --locked qmd-fast-server
      - name: Build the site
        run: qmd-fast build .          # website -> _site/   (a book emits _book/)
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with: { path: _site }

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deploy
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

`build` **executes code cells**, so if your pages run `{python}` / `{r}`, add a
step to install that interpreter plus `ipykernel` / `IRkernel` and set
`QMD_FAST_PYTHON` / `QMD_FAST_R` — otherwise those cells render as source in CI.

::: {.callout-note}
The interactive Observable/Three.js demos fetch their runtimes from a CDN and
need to be served over `http(s)` (not opened from `file://`). Once deployed — or
under `preview` — they are fully live.
:::
